rules.statement: When a query must exclude rows related to a variable set of other rows, express it as one server-side subquery predicate (e.g. `!db.Set.Any(...)`) instead of pre-reading the set and appending one `Where` clause per item.
rules.why: Per-item predicates make the SQL and its parameter count grow with the data, slow every page and can exceed provider limits, which can stop a platform-wide background sweep.
rules.check: Look for a loop that adds `.Where(...)` per element of a previously loaded list, or a lookup list re-read on every page of a paged query.

rules.statement: In a background loop that isolates each item's failure with try/catch, put all per-item work, including store reads done before the main work, inside the try.
rules.why: An exception thrown outside the per-item try leaves the loop, ends the pass for every remaining item and is not logged against the item that caused it.
rules.check: In a foreach with a per-item try/catch and failure log, look for awaited store or I/O calls for that item placed before the try.

rules.statement: Compare identifiers in code with the same case sensitivity that the store uses to look them up; if the store matches a normalized (case-insensitive) id, don't use `StringComparison.Ordinal` for guard checks on that id.
rules.why: A guard that compares case-sensitively while the lookup is case-insensitive can be bypassed with a differently cased id that still resolves to the protected entity.
rules.check: Look for `Ordinal` or `==` comparisons of route or user-supplied ids against a protected or configured id when the store resolves ids through a normalized column.

rules.statement: Declare an `.Produces(...)` on a minimal API endpoint for every non-2xx status code its handler documents or returns, unless a group-level convention already declares it.
rules.why: Otherwise the OpenAPI document leaves out those responses and generated clients never see them.
rules.check: Compare the status codes in the handler's XML docs and return paths (403, 404, 409, …) with the `.Produces` calls in the route mapping.

rules.statement: When processing a page of items that each need related data, fetch that related data once per page with a batched query (e.g. GetMany over the page's keys) instead of one query per item.
rules.why: Per-item queries add round trips that grow linearly with the number of items.
rules.check: Look for an awaited store call inside a per-item loop over a page whose keys could be gathered and read in one call.

rules.statement: Reuse data a method has already loaded, such as a lineage or a parent entity, instead of resolving each piece again through the store.
rules.why: Re-resolving data already in hand turns one read into dozens of queries per operation.
rules.check: Look for loops that call a store-backed resolve or count method for each element of a collection the method just read.

rules.statement: Don't report per-level store round trips in a recursive cache-miss walk up a hierarchy that stops at the first cached ancestor, and don't propose a lineage-first read in its place.
rules.why: Such a walk usually reads only the missing leaf, while a lineage-first read costs more queries in that common case.
rules.check: Before reporting, confirm whether the recursion returns at the first cache hit and what the proposed bulk read costs when only the leaf is missing.

rules.statement: Don't report an entity as loaded several times in one operation when the callers share one DbContext and the store's lookup checks `DbSet.Local` (the change tracker) before querying.
rules.why: Later lookups then come from the change tracker, so the row is read from the database only once.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the callers share a store manager or DbContext and whether the lookup method consults `DbSet.Local` first.

rules.statement: Don't report a `TryAdd*` service registration as unused or duplicate when a service that same registration method registers depends on it through its constructor.
rules.why: The registration lets that registration method work when no other group is added, and `TryAdd*` registrations of the same implementation cannot drift apart.
rules.check: Trace the constructor dependencies of the services the registration method adds, and check that the duplicates are all `TryAdd*` with the same implementation.

rules.statement: Don't ask to share a private page-size constant or the standard do/while PageRequest/NextCursor paging loop across classes, especially classes in assemblies that don't reference each other.
rules.why: Each batch size is tuned for the read of the loop that declares it, and the paging loop is the store idiom every caller writes.
rules.check: Before reporting duplication, check whether the constant is private to its loop and whether the classes share an assembly reference.

rules.statement: Have a helper return the results it produces, such as validation errors, instead of appending them to a mutable list the caller passes in, and group paired parameters (e.g. current and new values) into a record struct.
rules.why: Side effects on an argument are hidden, and long parameter lists are hard to read.
rules.check: Look for helper methods that take a `List<T>` parameter only to `Add` to it, or that take several parameters that always travel as a pair.

rules.statement: Assign a service or store lookup result (e.g. `GetStore<T>()`) to a local before calling it, rather than chaining the call onto the lookup.
rules.why: It is easier to read and matches how sibling code assigns stores to locals.
rules.check: Look for `GetStore<...>().Method(...)` chains.

rules.statement: Assign a conditionally built argument (e.g. a ternary choosing between two constructed values) to a local before passing it, instead of building it inline in the call's argument list.
rules.why: It is easier to read and to debug.
rules.check: Look for ternaries or factory calls that build a value inline in the arguments of an awaited call.

rules.statement: When the same decision rule (e.g. which authorization node to use, or how to build a revision lineage) appears in more than one place, extract one shared helper and call it from every site.
rules.why: Copies drift apart and then authorize at different points, or caches disagree about the state they were built from.
rules.check: Look for the same conditional or traversal logic repeated across methods or classes in the diff.

rules.statement: Store collections held in shared cache state or eviction-callback state as immutable collections (e.g. `ImmutableArray<T>`), not as a `List<T>` exposed through `IReadOnlyList<T>`.
rules.why: A cast back to `List<T>` could change shared cache state.
rules.check: Look for `List<T>` values stored in caches or in callback state and typed as read-only interfaces.

rules.statement: In client-side query caching, have a mutation invalidate a tag keyed by the entity itself, which the list queries provide for each item, instead of relying on optional caller-supplied parent ids to invalidate the parent's list.
rules.why: A caller that omits the parent id or passes a stale one leaves lists showing renamed or deleted items.
rules.check: Look for optional mutation arguments used only in `invalidatesTags`.

rules.statement: In tests, assert the behavior the test's name claims (e.g. that a cache is invalidated or refetched), not only incidental effects such as the URL or that no error occurred.
rules.why: Otherwise removing the behavior leaves the test passing.
rules.check: Compare the test name with its assertions; for invalidation tests, check that a cache is primed and its refetch is asserted, along with a negative case.

rules.statement: In a test project, when the code under test catches and logs per-item exceptions, don't rely on a strict mock throwing to fail the test; assert directly that no failure was logged (e.g. with FakeLogger) or that the work never ran.
rules.why: The production catch swallows the strict-mock exception, so the test claims more than it checks.
rules.check: Look for tests or comments that say touching a mock fails the test when the code path wraps the work in try/catch with logging.

rules.statement: In a test project, create Moq mocks through the test base's MockRepository that is verified on dispose, and mark the expected setups `.Verifiable()`, rather than calling `new Mock<T>(...)` directly.
rules.why: Mocks created outside the verified repository are never verified, so a setup that is never hit fails no test.
rules.check: Look for `new Mock<` in test files, and for setups without `.Verifiable()` on mocks whose calls are expected.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't report a null-forgiving `!` that passes a deliberate null to an argument-validation test.
rules.why: Test conventions allow that one use of the null-forgiving operator.
rules.check: Before reporting a `!` in a test, check whether it passes a deliberate null in an argument-validation test.

rules.statement: Before reporting a missing test case, search the project's other test files for the class under test, including files the pull request doesn't touch.
rules.why: The requested case often already exists in a sibling test file, such as a lifecycle test next to a hierarchy test.
rules.check: Search the test project for tests of the same method before reporting it as untested.

rules.statement: Don't ask an ADR to list another record as amended when it only describes how it composes with that record without changing that record's decision; citing it in References is enough.
rules.why: The Status line lists only the records whose decisions the ADR changes.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing amends entry, check whether the ADR actually changes the other record's decision.
